candidates.paper: Mechanical Tension Controls Granulation Tissue Contractile Activity and Myofibroblast Differentiation
candidates.causal_root: rat wounds splinted for 7 days then released for 1-2 days; separate 14-day granuloma pouches released from tension

notes.C3: Tension is physically removed and tissue contractility is measured, but the imposed/local wound mechanical state is not quantitatively mapped before and after release in the same strict sense required by the frozen clock protocol.
notes.C4: alpha-SMA falls 2-3 days after release; F-actin and ED-A fibronectin decline on a temporally ordered schedule.
notes.C5: No final scar-quality or tissue-function rescue with demonstrated preservation of wound integrity is provided.

candidates.paper: A modified scar model with controlled tension on secondary wound healing in mice
candidates.causal_root: granulation established by day 7, then controlled external tension applied for 14 days

notes.C3: Applied tension is explicitly quantified in N/mm^2 and adjustable in real time.
notes.C4: No qualifying same-state alpha-SMA/myofibroblast trajectory was identified in the reported experiment.
notes.C5: The model intentionally increases scar/collagen and high tension can injure tissue; it is not a delayed beneficial retuning experiment with preserved repair integrity.

candidates.notes: Primary anti-scarring treatment begins at wounding and is molecular rather than direct physical retuning. Repeated dosing can also delay closure, so it is retained as a timing/safety falsifier rather than admitted mechanics-clock evidence.

candidates.paper: Mussel Inspired Hydrogel Promotes Axon Regeneration via Piezo1 Modulation and Cytoskeleton Dynamics in Synergy After Spinal Cord Injury
candidates.notes: Strong causal mechanical-state study, but implantation occurs at injury rather than after lesion/scar establishment; axonal readouts do not constitute a delayed endogenous scar-state EXIT trajectory under this strict protocol.

candidates.paper: Mechanical Environment Afforded by Engineered Hydrogel Critically Regulates Survival of Neural Stem Cells Transplanted in the Injured Spinal Cord via Piezo1-Mediated Mechanotransduction
candidates.notes: NSC+hydrogel transplantation is delayed to 7 days and material stiffness is controlled, but no qualifying before/after endogenous lesion physical-state trajectory is established; primary causal endpoint is exogenous graft survival, not endogenous scar resolution or a qualifying whole-tissue structural/functional repair endpoint.

candidates.paper: Spinal Cord Injury Results in Chronic Mechanical Stiffening
candidates.notes: Chronic lesion stiffness is quantitatively measured, but the IMP intervention is acute (2, 24 and 48 h) and immune-directed rather than a delayed direct physical retuning. Function reported from separate prior work is not fused into this root.

candidates.paper: Timing effect of intramyocardial hydrogel injection for positively impacting left ventricular remodeling after myocardial infarction
candidates.notes: Hydrogel is injected at immediate, day-3 and 2-week phases and day 3 gives the strongest functional effect. However, no qualifying same-root before/after endogenous scar mechanical-state measurement and no state-specific longitudinal myofibroblast trajectory satisfying the frozen protocol were identified.

candidates.paper: The beneficial effects of deferred delivery on the efficiency of hydrogel therapy post myocardial infarction
candidates.notes: One-week deferred PEG injection improves scar thickness and ventricular function versus immediate delivery, but lacks the same-root endogenous tissue mechanics and same-state cellular trajectory required for admission.

candidates.paper: Temporal inhibition of ADAM17 in fibroblasts reduces stiffness and promotes vascularization following myocardial infarction
candidates.notes: A highly informative timing/mechanotransduction control. Short-term post-MI pharmacological inhibition targets the myofibroblast phase and improves long-term remodeling, while genetic myofibroblast Adam17 loss reduces scar stiffness. Under the root-integrity rule these arms are not fused: ADAM17 inhibition is biochemical rather than direct physical retuning, and stiffness evidence from the genetic root does not satisfy C3 for the delayed pharmacological root.

candidates.paper: Selective targeting of lysyl oxidase-like 2 (LOXL2) suppresses hepatic fibrosis progression and accelerates its reversal
candidates.notes: Closest strict root in the current ledger. Anti-LOXL2 begins after established bridging fibrosis, directly reduces collagen crosslink stabilization, and accelerates septal disruption during recovery. It is not admitted because a qualifying primary organ-function/regenerative outcome with the frozen repair-integrity requirement is absent.

falsification_controls.finding: Higher-stiffness 15% GelMA outperformed 7.5% GelMA for axonal extension and sensory recovery in one SCI model.
In infarcted heart, alpha-SMA myofibroblast state can decline while scar stiffness/collagen complexity continues to mature.
falsification_controls.consequence: Mechanical maturation and myofibroblast-state abundance are not interchangeable clocks.

closest_missing_measurements.SKIN: Delayed tension/offloading after established alpha-SMA with quantitative local tissue mechanics before/after plus final scar strength/architecture and wound-integrity outcome in the same root.
closest_missing_measurements.SPINAL_CORD: Delayed endogenous lesion mechanical retuning after measured scar/lesion establishment, followed by repeated lesion mechanics, endogenous scar-state trajectory and whole-tissue functional recovery in the same root.
closest_missing_measurements.HEART: Delayed direct physical/crosslink retuning after scar stabilization with same-arm scar modulus/crosslink readout, lineage-resolved fibroblast-state trajectory and rupture/remodeling/function endpoints.
